metadata.title: enterprise-search
metadata.purpose: Answer whether one search is enough to get an answer from a company's own knowledge, using the enterprise-search skill (Glean Client REST API) as the concrete case. Lands the carry-out that enterprise search is a three-step loop — search for candidates, read the document, report what you used — not a single lookup.
metadata.anchor_pair: B01 -> B05 (the contractor-onboarding question: snippet found, full document read, feedback filed)

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes Claude just searches the company's docs and answers straight from the results. It's closer to this: search finds candidates, reading the document is what actually answers you. Liam — take them through it.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'Does Claude just search our docs and answer from the results?', hesitates on 'results', corrects to 'documents', lands the real question

props.text:
Does Claude just search
our docs and answer
from the results?

beats.narration_text: Say you ask: what's our policy on contractor onboarding, and is there a prior decision already on file? Answering that means reaching into the company's own knowledge — chat, drives, tickets, wikis — not the open web.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — the onboarding question, with chat/drives/tickets/wikis fanning into one shared index

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — one question, many sources
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. The onboarding question types onto the card. Four source chips — CHAT, DRIVES, TICKETS, WIKIS — fan in from the corners and converge into one labelled INDEX box. THIS EXACT QUESTION RETURNS AT B05.

beats.narration_text: The easy assumption: run one search, and the top result already has the answer. But a search result is a snippet — about thirty-five words, just enough to judge whether a document is worth opening. It was never built to answer anything by itself.

shot.new_visual_element: A search box returns a truncated snippet card; 'IS THE ANSWER' struck through

production_viz.label: A snippet, not an answer
production_viz.mechanic: A search box yields one result card: a snippet of text trailing into an ellipsis. Overlaid text 'THE ANSWER?' appears, then is struck through in terracotta. A caption settles beneath: '~35 words — built to triage, not to answer.'

beats.narration_text: The loop runs in three steps. Search returns ranked snippets across every connected source. Read fetches the full text of the documents that matter, using the IDs from search. Feedback — upvote what you used, downvote what you rejected — trains the ranker, and it happens before the task is called done. Two bundled scripts handle the busy work: one for searching with pagination, one for reading up to fifty documents at a time.

props.sparkLine: Search finds candidates. Read gets the answer. Feedback trains the ranker.

beats.narration_text: Two rules keep it honest. Always search the shared index first — it already ranks across every source, dedupes, and respects permissions — before falling back to one connector directly. And pagination is cursor-based: pass the cursor back exactly as given, never build one yourself, stop when there isn't one. One catch: an empty result can mean two different things — the content genuinely isn't indexed, or the identity asking simply can't see it. The API doesn't say which.

props.sparkLine: Index first. Never build a cursor. Empty can mean no access.

beats.narration_text: Back to the onboarding question: search turns up a snippet that mentions a policy — that's step one. Reading the full document is what actually surfaces the exception buried in the next paragraph. Marking that document as used is step three, and it's what makes tomorrow's search better.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — the onboarding question, snippet found, full document opened, exception surfaced, feedback filed

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — snippet, document, feedback
production_viz.mechanic: THE B01 QUESTION RETURNS, identical. A snippet card appears (step 1), then opens into a full document with one line — the exception — highlighted in terracotta (step 2). A checkmark chip 'used' files against the document (step 3).

beats.narration_text: Finding something doesn't mean you have the whole picture — some sources might not be connected yet. And finding nothing doesn't mean the answer doesn't exist — it might be a permissions gap, or a query that needs to broaden before you conclude that.

shot.new_visual_element: Mirrored panels: FOUND (not the whole picture) / EMPTY (not proof it's missing)

production_viz.label: Found isn't complete. Empty isn't proof.
production_viz.mechanic: Two mirrored panels. Left: 'FOUND' with an arrow to 'THE WHOLE PICTURE' — struck through, caption 'some sources aren't connected yet'. Right: 'EMPTY' with an arrow to 'DOESN'T EXIST' — struck through, caption 'permissions gap, or broaden the query'.

beats.narration_text: Enterprise search isn't one lookup — it's search for candidates, read the document that matters, then say what you used, so the next search ranks better.

props.quote: Enterprise search isn't one lookup — it's search for candidates, read the document that matters, then say what you used, so the next search ranks better.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me: Search our internal docs for our policy on contractor onboarding. Read the full document, not just the snippet, and tell me if there's a prior decision on file. Then tell me what you used to answer, before you finish. Liam, in for Bear.
